problem_statement:
Build a brand-new /pricing page from scratch for the Gatsby Serif business theme. The route /pricing does not exist yet (baseline serves an empty document). Create src/pages/pricing.js as a real Gatsby page that (1) reuses the site's shared so it carries the exact same chrome as the existing /services and /team pages — the header logo, the main navigation (Services, Team, About, Contact) and the footer titled 'Gatsby Serif Theme'; (2) renders an intro block with an

Pricing Plans

and a lead paragraph; (3) shows three pricing tiers (Starter, Professional, Enterprise) built from an INLINE static data array (no network fetch), each tier a reusable card with an

plan name, a per-month price, a short tagline and a 'Choose ' call-to-action link into /contact/; (4) provides a real monthly / annual billing toggle: two buttons carrying data-billing="monthly" and data-billing="annual", and a billing-note paragraph that must switch from 'Billed monthly, cancel anytime.' to 'Billed annually — save 20% compared to monthly.' when Annual is selected (prices update too). The page must reuse the theme's colors/typography/spacing (bootstrap grid, .strip/.container/.feature classes, Playfair Display headings, #8036ca primary) and must not overflow horizontally on a 390px mobile viewport.
required_content: An intro block with h1.title 'Pricing Plans' and a lead paragraph describing the plans
Shared site chrome from <Layout>: header logo, main nav (Services / Team / About / Contact) and the footer titled 'Gatsby Serif Theme' — identical to /services and /team
A monthly/annual billing toggle: a 'Monthly' button (data-billing=monthly) and an 'Annual' button (data-billing=annual)
A billing-note paragraph reading 'Billed monthly, cancel anytime.' in the default (monthly) state
Three pricing tiers from an inline data array: Starter, Professional, Enterprise
Each tier rendered as a .feature card with an h3 plan name, a per-month price line, a tagline paragraph and a 'Choose <plan>' button-primary link to /contact/
Interaction: selecting Annual updates the billing note to 'Billed annually — save 20% compared to monthly.' and lowers the displayed prices
design_constraints: Reuse the existing shared <Layout> component (Header + Menu nav + Footer + SubFooter) — do NOT re-implement the chrome; the new page must be visually and structurally consistent with the sibling /services and /team pages
Reuse the theme design tokens: bootstrap grid (container/row/col), .strip strip-grey band, .feature card, .title heading, .button / .button-primary, Playfair Display headings, #8036ca primary color

Match the reference color palette exactly so the page reads as part of the theme: primary/action color #8036ca (rgb(128,54,202)) on white (#ffffff); body text #212529 (rgb(33,37,41)); muted/secondary text #5c5a5a (rgb(92,90,90)); the h1.title heading color #2f2f41 (rgb(47,47,65)); .button and .button-primary use a #8036ca fill with white text and 4px border-radius
Typography: the h1.title uses Playfair Display at ~50px/700 weight; card h3 plan names use the sans-serif stack at ~20px/700 weight; body copy 16px/400
Pricing data must be inlined as a static array in the page (no fetch / no GraphQL data source)
author_notes: 方案A. baseline: src/pages/pricing.js = empty stub (<></>, no Layout) so the clean-URL static server resolves /pricing/ to an empty document instead of falling back to home (gotcha #18k); route genuinely missing. reference: full pricing page reusing shared <Layout> (cross-page consistency chrome) + monthly/annual toggle + inline data. bad: byte-identical structure/content AND full shared Layout (so dom + cross-page consistency PASS), but the billing-note is hardcoded to the monthly copy and prices never change → the Annual click produces no observable delta → fails ONLY interaction_assertions. Reference passes 19/19. Cross-page consistency asserted by requiring the footer h3 'Gatsby Serif Theme' + nav links Services/Team on BOTH desktop_pricing and the sibling desktop_services state. Three source trees md5-distinct (only src/pages/pricing.js differs). Offline: gatsby build succeeds with NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider (capture sets this by default); google-fonts + google-analytics offline fetches covered by console_error_allowlist.
